01Project overview

Most reports arrived by phone, not through the web form

The problem

DC Water has a web form for reporting problems, but most reports come in through the emergency hotline. That leads to a high volume of calls and slower response times.

DC Water distributes drinking water and collects and treats wastewater for residents and visitors of the District of Columbia. Its web form lets people report issues such as leaks and broken fire hydrants, so customers and DC Water can resolve problems in homes and neighborhoods together.

Design challenge

DC Water wants to drive users to its mobile-responsive web form and make reporting problems more efficient.

My role and the team's work

At the end of Sprint 2 the team changed, and I was one of the members who joined the project midway through the semester. Because I joined at the beginning of Sprint 3, this case study focuses on Sprints 3–5 only.

My contributions

  • Conducted card sorting activities, user interviews, user testing, and prototyping.
  • Worked on the visual and interactive designs.
  • As facilitator of Sprint 4, directed the course of the project, oversaw the schedule, and led client presentations.
  • In Sprint 5, the team divided the work and I worked only on the image recognition concept.

Team process

  • The team of six worked in five 4-week sprints based on the Google Ventures Design Sprint process.
  • Each sprint covered research and analysis, ideation, design, evaluation, and refinement.
  • Research, design iterations, and testing described below were carried out as a team ("we") unless noted as mine.

02Solution preview

Report a problem, receive updates, and track it to resolution

The redesigned Report a Problem form separates water problems from general inquiries, lets people choose how they hear back, and gives every report a trackable ticket.

01 · Report
Plain-language choices

People locate the problem, then pick from everyday categories such as Flooding / Leaking or Damage, with an Other / Not Sure option.

02 · Receive updates
Notifications on their terms

Separate choices for receiving updates about the ticket and for letting DC Water get in touch with questions, by phone call or email.

03 · Track
Ticket status and details

A status bar, case history, and the details of what was submitted, plus a way to rate the experience once the case is resolved.
